description.narrative: Our Voices Our Futures (OVOF) partners bring extensive experience of lobbying and advocacy at multiple levels to a range of issues connecting ground-level evidence and lived realities of structurally silenced women feed directly into lobbying and advocacy at every level and internationally at the six countries. More international and national-level law and policymakers need to acknowledge and address the issue of growing authoritarianism (and its impact on civic space, democracy and the lives of structurally silenced women) and the increasing influence of anti-gender and anti-rights actors within international and national policy and legal spaces. Key Dutch actorswill be mobilised to collaborate with and support Women Human Rights Defenders, LBT activists, and sex workers’ rights movements by creating and opening spaces for their participation in internationalprocesses such as the Commission on the Status of Women and Human Rights Council so that their voices will be heard.

We aim to do 1 capacity-building workshop for structurally silenced women in Uganda to build their capacity in policy advocacy.

APC partner in Uganda conducted a capacity-building workshop for structurally silenced women to build skills on policy advocacy. They worked with 13 LBT and sex worker organisations. Participants learnt how to plan advocacy campaigns and develop strategies for the same.

APC aims to work with 2 CSOs in Uganda to build their capacity of digital policy advocacy and internet governance, and on how this intersects with rights of structurally silenced women in the online space. This will be done through capacity building workshops in each of the countries.

Partners in Uganda held digital security and feminist technology workshops and webinars both in person as well as on online. The online convenings allowed more CSOs to attend the workshop safely, especially in light of the new anti-homosexuality laws in Uganda, and for more spaces to be created easily.
